messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Parsing functions index
parts:
Can someone test the attached .sh file on a Mac? It needs the environmental variable STAN_HOME to be defined and then (for me) parses stan-reference.idx into a tab-delimited file that looks like

goodrich@T540p:/tmp$ head stan-reference.txt
StanFunction     Arguments       ReturnType      Page
abs     (int x) int     272
abs     (real x)        real    281
acosh   (real x)        real    286
acos    (real x)        real    285
append_col      (matrix x, matrix y)    matrix  314
append_col      (matrix x, vector y)    matrix  314
append_col      (row_vector x, row_vector y)    row_vector      315
append_col      (vector x, matrix y)    matrix  315
append_col      (vector x, vector y)    matrix  315

which can be read into R (or other interfaces) with the .R attachment to create a lookup table between the function(s) in the interface and the Stan function(s).

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Parsing functions index
parts:
The sed on Mac is not GNU sed. This sed does not support -i to do in-place editing.

see
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5694228/sed-in-place-flag-that-works-both-on-mac-bsd-and-linux

Jiqiang

> Can someone test the attached .sh file on a Mac? It needs the environmental

>

> StanFunction Arguments ReturnType Page
> abs (int x) int 272
> abs (real x) real 281
> acosh (real x) real 286
> acos (real x) real 285
> append_col (matrix x, matrix y) matrix 314
> append_col (matrix x, vector y) matrix 314
> append_col (row_vector x, row_vector y) row_vector 315
> append_col (vector x, matrix y) matrix 315
> append_col (vector x, vector y) matrix 315
>
> which can be read into R (or other interfaces) with the .R attachment to
> create a lookup table between the function(s) in the interface and the Stan
> function(s).
>
> Ben

> #! /bin/bash -e
>
> cd $STAN_HOME
> make manual
>
> cd $STAN_HOME/src/docs/stan-reference
> SRI="stan-reference.txt"
> cp stan-reference.idx $SRI
>
> sed -i 's/^\\indexentry{{\\tt \\bfseries //g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/ }!{\\tt /;/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/{\\tt \\slshape //g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/:.*em}/;/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/}|hyperpage}{/;/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/ }!sampling statement|hyperpage}{/;~;real;/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/}//g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/\\_/_/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/^ //g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/"\(.*\)"/\1/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/"!/!/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/{\\\&\\\&/\&\&/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/{//g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/\\textasciicircum/\^/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/\\textbackslash /\\/g' $SRI
> sed -i 's/@.*(/;(/g' $SRI
> sort $SRI > stan-reference-temp.txt
> mv stan-reference-temp.txt $SRI
> sed -i '1i StanFunction; Arguments; ReturnType; Page' $SRI
> sed -i 's/;/\t/g' $SRI
> exit 0

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Parsing functions index
parts:
Pipe is fine. But not tab, so I think you can just use semicolon.
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5398395/how-can-i-insert-a-tab-character-with-sed-on-os-x


Also, the `sed '1i ...'` works differently. I think the following can be used instead:

echo 'StanFunction; Arguments; ReturnType; Page' > $TEMP
cat $SRI >> $TEMP

Attached is the one that seems to work on Mac.

Jiqiang

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Parsing functions index
parts:
On Saturday, January 17, 2015 at 4:12:06 PM UTC-5, Jeffrey Arnold wrote:

It definitely helps. Thanks Ben! I don't know why I didn't parse the idx. I was using similar regexes to parse a hand edited file generated from pdftotext. The only upside of that approach is it keeps the descriptions of the functions and the section they're in, but those aren't that important.

Since there is a column for the page number in the Stan manual, people could easily look up the function definition if necessary. But the use case I more had in mind was when the user knows what the function is in R (i.e. cbind) and needs to figure out what the corresponding Stan function is (i.e. append_col). Possibly someone could do a reverse lookup as well.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Parsing functions index
parts:
I think it will be fine as long as it doesn't introduce the need for new regexes (and if we do need to add new regexes, it is not really a big deal).

But I am not a fan of having aliases for Stan functions or adding things to the Stan index that are not actually Stan functions, especially since rbind and cbind are R specific and do not correspond to any other Stan interface. What Andrew should have requested is exactly what I am proposing in the PR and what I am then planning to add to the next RStan, where you can just do something like this in R

stan_lookup(RFunction = "rbind")
[1] "append_row"

Ben
